narrationTexts: I'll start by looking at the project files.
I'll switch the map to channel lists so a priority can fan out.
Quiet hours span midnight, so I'll compute it as an hour check.
Dedup needs the scratch state, so I'll put a per-key last-sent map in `createState()`.
finalText:
Done. The dedup keys off the state map:

```js
const lastSentAt = state.lastSentAt.get(event.key);
if (lastSentAt !== undefined && event.at - lastSentAt < DEDUP_WINDOW_MINUTES) {
  return [];
}
// ...decide channels...
state.lastSentAt.set(event.key, event.at);
```

Three behaviors worth calling out, all verified:

```
at=600 a -> ["email"]     at=700 c -> ["email"]     at=800 d -> ["pager"]
at=602 a -> []            at=702 c -> []            at=802 d -> []
at=604 a -> []            at=705 c -> ["email"]
at=605 a -> ["email"]
at=603 b -> ["email"]     (other keys unaffected)
```

- The clock only restarts on an actual send — a suppressed repeat doesn't extend the window, so a flapping key still gets through every 5 minutes instead of being silenced forever.
- Critical dedups like everything else. You said "if we already sent something with the same key," with no priority carve-out; say the word if pages should always go through.
- Queued (quiet-hours) notifications count as sent, since they did go somewhere.
- Boundary: a repeat exactly 5 minutes later delivers (`at=605` above) — the window is strictly under 5.

Replay: 0 errors, 99 dropped, which is exactly the flap count `events.js` injects (every 9th event, minus `i=0` which has no predecessor). Pager fell 225 → 200 and queue 300 → 266 as those repeats fell out.
